definitions.explanation: The body of law governing commercial transactions and businesses; in Japan, one of the Six Codes. Also used loosely to mean a particular way of doing business.

examples.japanese: {商法|しょうほう}を{改正|かいせい}する。
{会社|かいしゃ}の{設立|せつりつ}は{商法|しょうほう}に{基|もと}づいて{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: The establishment of a company is carried out based on the commercial code.

examples.japanese: {強引|ごういん}な{勧誘|かんゆう}をする{悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう}に{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: Please be careful of unscrupulous business practices that use forceful solicitation.

notes:
Composed of {商|しょう} (commerce) + {法|ほう} (law). As one of the Six Codes, it governs merchants, companies, and commercial transactions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {商法|しょうほう}{改正|かいせい}: revision of the commercial code
- {会社法|かいしゃほう}: the Companies Act — split off from the commercial code in 2005
- {悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう}: unscrupulous / fraudulent business practices

USAGE:
Beyond the statute, {商法|しょうほう} is often used in the sense of a "way of doing business," especially in the fixed phrase {悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう} (shady sales tactics).
